question: What is a common cause of accidental poisoning among toddlers at home?

options.D: Stored kerosene in soft drink bottles

explanation: Kerosene is frequently kept in clear beverage containers. This makes it resemble drinking water to young children who may swallow it by mistake. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h1)

question: Why is knowing how a poison entered the body important in emergency care?

options.A: It helps the laboratory test blood sugar accurately
options.B: It proves whether the patient took the poison on purpose
options.C: It tells the exact financial cost of hospital treatment
options.D: It shows how fast the toxin spreads and guides early management

explanation: Different entry routes, such as swallowing, breathing, or skin contact, change how quickly the poison enters the bloodstream and dictate the necessary first aid steps. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h1)

question: What is the very first priority for a nurse arriving at a poisoning scene?

options.A: Ensuring the safety of the environment
options.B: Writing down the exact time of exposure
options.C: Washing the patient's skin with soap

explanation: A nurse cannot help anyone if they also become overcome by toxic fumes or dangerous substances at the scene. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h2)

question: An unconscious patient who has swallowed a poison is breathing on their own. What position should they be placed in?
explanation: The recovery position keeps the airway clear and prevents vomit or saliva from entering the lungs if the patient vomits while unconscious. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h2)

question: Which traditional practice for swallowed poisons is dangerous and should be discouraged?

options.A: Inducing vomiting with palm oil or salt water
options.B: Bringing the empty container to the clinic
options.C: Flushing splashed eyes with clean saline
options.D: Washing the skin with soap and running water

explanation: Making a patient vomit can cause the poison to burn the throat a second time or enter the lungs, leading to severe pneumonia. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h3)

question: Why must you avoid scrubbing the skin too hard when washing off chemical contaminants?

options.A: It can break the skin barrier and increase toxin absorption
options.B: It wastes too much clean water in the emergency ward
options.C: It makes the chemical change into a stronger poison
options.D: It stops the soap from creating enough foam

explanation: Damaging the outer layer of the skin opens up pathways for chemicals to enter the bloodstream much faster. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h3)

question: What pupil size is typically seen in a patient with acute organophosphate poisoning?
explanation: Organophosphates overstimulate the parasympathetic nervous system, leading to constricted, pinpoint pupils. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h4)

question: An emergency patient presents with confusion, flushed skin, high fever, and very dry skin. Which toxicdrome fits these signs?
explanation: These classic signs describe the anticholinergic toxicdrome, often remembered by the phrases hot as a hare, blind as a bat, and dry as a bone. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h4)

question: Which medication is given as an antidote for organophosphate poisoning to dry up secretions?
explanation: Atropine blocks specific receptors to dry up excessive saliva, sweat, and bronchial secretions caused by organophosphates. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of giving activated charcoal after a poison is swallowed?

options.A: To force the patient to vomit out the poison quickly
options.B: To bind and hold onto the toxin in the gut to prevent absorption
options.C: To neutralize acid burns inside the stomach lining
options.D: To put the patient to sleep during emergency procedures

explanation: Activated charcoal has a large surface area that traps chemicals on its surface, stopping them from entering the bloodstream from the digestive tract. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h5)

question: What is a major preventative measure against childhood poisoning in the home?

options.A: Transferring bug spray into empty juice bottles
options.B: Throwing expired medicines into open household dustbins
options.C: Keeping traditional herbal mixtures open on the kitchen floor
options.D: Storing chemicals and medications in locked high cabinets

explanation: Keeping toxic substances locked away and out of the sight and reach of crawling infants and toddlers stops most accidental ingestions. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h6)

question: Why is it unsafe to keep household chemicals in old beverage bottles?

options.A: The local environmental health officers will fine the family
options.B: The chemical eats through the plastic and spills on the floor
options.C: It changes the color of the liquid so adults cannot use it
options.D: Children easily mistake them for drinks and swallow them

explanation: Using beverage bottles for dangerous items removes visual warnings, leading toddlers to drink them thinking it is water or juice. [learn more](BMP110_U7_T6#BMP110_U7_T6_h6)
